parts:
Here’s the easiest step-by-step way to start a GoFundMe:

1. Go to GoFundMe and tap **Start a GoFundMe**. GoFundMe says it will guide you through prompts to set up the fundraiser. citeturn117032search1turn117032search3

2. Choose **where the funds will go** and **who you’re fundraising for**. You’ll select whether the money is for yourself, someone else, or a charity, and the withdrawal location sets the currency collected. citeturn117032search0

3. Create your account. You can sign up with Google, Facebook, Apple, or your email address. GoFundMe notes that the name you enter is shown publicly, while your legal name is used later for transfers. citeturn117032search0

4. Add your fundraiser title and story. GoFundMe recommends a clear title and a story of at least 100 words that explains who needs help, what happened, how the money will be used, and why support matters. citeturn117032search0turn117032search6

5. Upload a photo or video. GoFundMe includes this as part of setup, and a real, clear image usually helps people trust the fundraiser more. citeturn117032search3

6. Set your fundraising goal. GoFundMe lets you choose your own goal and says it can be changed later if needed. citeturn117032search0turn117032search3

7. Publish the fundraiser and set up bank transfers. GoFundMe recommends getting your transfer setup done early so donations can be withdrawn smoothly. citeturn117032search6turn117032search7

8. Share it right away. GoFundMe specifically recommends sharing by text, email, and social media, and continuing to post it more than once. citeturn117032search3turn117032search6

9. Post updates within the first week. Keeping people updated can help build trust and keep momentum going. citeturn117032search6

A simple formula for your story:
- what happened
- why you need help now
- exactly what the money will cover
- how people can help, even if they can’t donate

Example title:
**Help [Name] Build a Safe Cat Sanctuary in Hawaii**

Example opening:
“Hi, my name is Bethany, and I’m raising money to help my sister and her husband create a safe sanctuary for abandoned and community cats on the Big Island. These funds will go toward food, medical care, building materials, bedding, and rescue supplies.”

For the goal amount, pick a number that covers the actual need without feeling random. If you need $3,000 to $5,000, I’d usually set it at **$5,000** so it gives enough room for supplies, care, and fees. GoFundMe notes there is a transaction fee per donation, so many people set the goal a bit higher than the exact need. citeturn117032search0

I can also write your full GoFundMe title, story, and first Facebook post for you.
